item.title: WEEK IN REVIEW: Kenya-China Ties Deepen as JKIA Expansion Begins and Exports Surge
item.description: Chinese Premier Li Qiang will travel to Southeast Asia starting tomorrow. He will pay an official state visit to Thailand on Friday and Saturday, before attending the China-ASEAN summit in the Philippines on 15 and 16 November. The latter visit comes amid ongoing tensions with …
item.dc:creator: CGSP Staff
item.content:encoded:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang will travel to Southeast Asia starting tomorrow. He will pay an official state visit to Thailand on Friday and Saturday, before attending the China-ASEAN summit in the Philippines on 15 and 16 November. The latter visit comes amid ongoing tensions with Manila. China’s Foreign Ministry name-checked the implementation of an upgraded China-ASEAN free trade protocol as a key priority for the gathering. (CHINESE FOREIGN MINISTRY)

China, Russia and the United States are reportedly discussing the agenda for mooted trilateral talks at the APEC summit in Shenzhen next week. The war in Ukraine and the denuclearization of the Korean peninsula have apparently “largely fallen off the table” as topics, in favor of those offering consensus. Controlling the use of AI in nuclear weapons systems and a joint statement against future nuclear war seem to be top contenders. (SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST)

Germany has reportedly banned the use of commercially available Chinese-made drones around its military bases as a security precaution. The move follows the United States’ ban on Chinese-made BYD electric vehicles at its base in Okinawa. Poland has imposed a similar ban. Der Spiegel reports that the military is withdrawing Chinese-made drones from service as quickly as possible and that they were bought without proper oversight. (THE GUARDIAN)

Somewhat contradictory reports have emerged about Volkswagen’s fortunes in China. Bloomberg reports that Volkswagen China has seen a rebound in sales, with a jump of 350% year on year, with several new models being released this year. It is a rare success for the company, which has faced increasing competition within China, pushing it from its earlier top status. However, Reuters reports that its electric vehicle joint venture in Anhui hasn’t planned any new models for 2027 and 2028 , and is falling further behind, amid limited uptake of its current offerings. (BLOOMBERG)

Xpeng, a Chinese manufacturer of low-altitude flying vehicles, said it would start rolling out flying cars for domestic sales in China within a few months. The rollout will reportedly start with limited partners, accelerating to a full commercial rollout by summer 2027. A two-seater will apparently set you back $300,000 and comes with a cockpit the size of a small car. (EURONEWS)

Sri Lanka has reportedly granted permission to a Chinese company to test a pilotless air taxi service. EHang reportedly got the green light from the Civil Aviation Authority to test a two-seater vertical takeoff and landing vehicle for commercial passenger use. This follows a demonstration flight that transported Ports and Aviation Minister Anura Karunathilaka as its first customer. (THE STRAITS TIMES)

Stanbic IBTC Bank announced this week that it is joining the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS), China’s alternative to the dollar-centric SWIFT system . CIPS facilitates cross-border trade in Chinese RMB, and the move is expected to facilitate already high Nigeria-China trade, pushed by thousands of small-scale traders and a robust e-commerce sector. It was facilitated by Stanbic’s parent company, South Africa’s Standard Bank, in which China’s ICBC has a minority share. (GUARDIAN NIGERIA)

Construction has started on an expansion of Kenya’s Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, led by China Road and Bridge Corporation. It follows the cancellation of an earlier contract with India’s Adani Group. Meanwhile, Kenyan exports to China reportedly jumped 60% year on year during the first three months of China’s recently announced zero-tariff African trade regime. Coffee and scrap copper reportedly led the charge. (HOTELIER BUZZ)

India’s Ministry of External Affairs complained about Chinese vloggers passing off footage filmed in impoverished areas of Bangladesh as depictions of India. “We have seen media reports in this regard. Such efforts to present a distorted picture of any country are unfortunate,” External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told reporters, referring to reports about Chinese influencers labeling images of Dhaka’s Uttara and Tekpara neighborhoods as Indian cityscapes. (HINDUSTAN TIMES)

Pakistan announced a major milestone in the construction of its Chashma 5 Nuclear power plant, with the facility’s dome being successfully installed. The project is led by China Zhongyuan Engineering Corporation. (CONSTRUCTION REVIEW)

The 9th China International Import Expo concluded in Shanghai on Tuesday with a record $85.45 billion in one-year intended deals, up 2.3% from the last edition . Among them, Kazakh oilseed processors signed $108 million in export agreements at the event, as the sector’s exports have grown fivefold over five seasons. ( CHINESE STATE COUNCIL )

Indonesia raised $1.5 billion in its second panda bond sale this year . It issued three-, five-, and seven-year yuan notes with coupons of 1.96% to 2.50% in China’s domestic market, with the goal of helping to finance its 2026 budget deficit. Bids were about 1.7 times the amount offered. Indonesia has now raised a total of $2.55 billion in panda bonds this year. ( REUTERS )

China concluded a three-week peacekeeping drone training course in Xi’an for developing countries . Trainees from China, the UN, and eight countries, including Algeria, Malaysia, and South Africa, attended the course, run by the Chinese defense ministry’s Peacekeeping Affairs Center and Air Force Engineering University. ( GLOBAL TIMES )

Saudi Arabia’s foreign trade authority has opened an anti-dumping investigation into steel imports from China and Türkiye, focusing on light and medium hot-rolled structural sections, angles, and shapes. The probe is meant to shield local industry from dumped or subsidized imports and to defend Saudi exports against potential trade remedies from other countries. ( ARAB NEWS )

Ukraine’s trade commission has launched an investigation into alleged circumvention of its 2023 anti-dumping duty of 32.6% on Chinese steel wire through Vietnam. The complainant’s lawyers say the wire was declared as Malaysian in 2024–2025, then as Vietnamese after duties were extended to Malaysia, with Vietnamese imports surging. ( NEW VOICE OF UKRAINE )

Industry and Trade Minister Ryad Mezzour told parliament that Morocco’s textile sector faces mounting pressure from foreign competitors, including Vietnam, shifting European market conditions, and expanding Chinese e-commerce platforms such as Shein. He said Europe faces the same platform-driven disruption, adding that efforts to address it are underway and could affect Morocco’s textile industry. ( MOROCCO WORLD NEWS )

Myanmar’s military government is courting U.S. investment in its rare earth deposits, pitching them as a way for Washington to reduce dependence on China, which processes most supply and makes about 90% of rare earth magnets. However, most output comes from areas outside the junta’s control, mainly Kachin state, where the Kachin Independence Army holds key mines. ( REUTERS )

Chinese coal buyers are resisting Indonesian miners’ efforts to rewrite 2027 contracts with waiver clauses that would excuse missed deliveries if Jakarta cuts output quotas or delays export approvals. As Indonesia prioritizes domestic power supply and routes exports through state channels, its coal shipments to China are down nearly 10% in the first 10 months from a year earlier. ( BLOOMBERG )

Ghana’s Minerals Commission warned Chinese nationals at a China-Ghana mining conference on Tuesday that illegal small-scale mining carries 20-25 years in prison plus deportation, and urged Beijing to help dismantle galamsey networks. It flagged “fronting” through Ghanaian entities and said a planned medium-scale category would let foreign investors, including Chinese, hold up to 40% stakes. ( MODERN GHANA )

Nigerian authorities uncovered a suspected Chinese-run illegal oil refinery in Ogun State, lacking a permit and able to store over 90,000 liters, after previously shutting down four illicit lithium plants. The case follows Ghana’s recent clampdowns on Chinese-linked illegal mining, though no link has been established. ( BUSINESS INSIDER AFRICA )

State-owned Sichuan Roads and Bridges Group has been named the developer of the proposed $389 million Mzima II pipeline, which would carry water 220 kilometers to Kenya’s coast under a 30-year build-operate-transfer concession. The project remains in the feasibility stage, with final construction clearance still pending. ( KENYA TODAY )

Power Minister Joseph Tegbe said on Monday that Nigeria will spend $2 billion on an East-West Super Grid to lift transmission capacity to at least 19,000 megawatts, with delivery expected in 18-24 months. Financing was not specified. It may be the same project Nigeria reportedly negotiated for the same amount with China’s Export-Import Bank last October, but that is unconfirmed. ( BUSINESSFRONT )

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla will visit China from this Tuesday to Friday as a special envoy of the Cuban Communist Party and government . Last week, the U.S. imposed sanctions on two Chinese companies it accused of supplying equipment and components to the Cuban military. ( CHINESE FOREIGN MINISTRY )

U.S. President Donald Trump says he expects to meet Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Nov. 18-19 to discuss ending the Iran war and denuclearization . The Wall Street Journal reports Putin wants to use a trilateral meeting to discuss the war in Ukraine. China and Russia have not yet confirmed the meeting. ( REUTERS )

China says it is willing to buy more liquefied natural gas from Papua New Guinea and deepen trade ties after Port Moresby moved to close Taiwan’s representative office . Taiwan alleged that Chinese pressure led to the closing of its office, and in response, Taiwan announced it would halt its own PNG gas purchases from PNG. ( REUTERS )

China’s NPC Standing Committee ratified the founding agreement for the World AI Cooperation Organization (WAICO), which Xi Jinping announced in July with 38 founding members. Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing will push the body toward physical operation, focus on practical cooperation and capacity-building in the Global South, and welcome more members. ( CHINESE FOREIGN MINISTRY )

Japan signed a $27 million deal Monday to give the Philippine Navy a coastal surveillance radar and the Air Force uncrewed aircraft. It is the first finished Japanese-made defense equipment transferred under Tokyo’s Official Security Assistance program, created in 2023 to help developing countries counter China’s growing influence. ( ASSOCIATED PRESS )

India is in final-stage talks to sell the Philippines about five BrahMos supersonic cruise missile systems, nearly 60 missiles, for $700-800 million, Indian sources say. The deal would dwarf Manila’s prior $375 million naval order as it bolsters coastal defenses amid South China Sea tensions. ( REUTERS )

China’s foreign ministry announced on Friday that Xi Jinping appointed six new ambassadors. Notably, Yao Fei replaced Zhou Limin as Chinese Ambassador to Kiribati, and Chen Haiping replaced Zhou Jian as Chinese Ambassador to Fiji. New ambassadors were also appointed to Norway, the Czech Republic, and New Zealand. ( CHINA’S FOREIGN MINISTRY )

A Pakistani astronaut will join China’s space station for this year’s Shenzhou-24 mission as part of cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative. This marks the first joint spaceflight featuring both Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s manned space program, according to CCTV. ( ASSOCIATED PRESS )

The U.S. imposed sanctions late last week on two Chinese companies it accused of supplying equipment and components to Cuba’s military . The companies are China National Electronic Import and Export Company and China Electronics Technology Group Corporation International. ( SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST )

Twenty-seven residents are suing COMMUS, a unit of Chinese miner Zijin Mining, at Kolwezi’s Commercial Court, seeking $6.3 million over alleged pollution-related health harm. Backed by RAID and AFREWATCH, the suit also names the Congolese state and regulator ACE for monitoring failures. Claimants want $1.3 million in compensation and $5 million for restoration. ( REUTERS )

A court in Serang fined Chinese-owned smelter PT Peter Metal Technology $110,400 for illegally handing radioactive Caesium-137 waste to an unauthorized third party in Banten. Its Chinese director, Lin Jingzhang, was sentenced to three years in prison and fined $2,760 in a separate November 3 verdict. Inability to pay could suspend operations. ( INDONESIA BUSINESS POST )

Chinese building materials firm Huaxin has agreed to buy 99.99% of CSN Cimentos, Brazil’s second-largest cement producer, for $1.64 billion, marking China’s first entry into the country’s cement market. The unit of steelmaker Companhia Siderúrgica Nacional holds roughly 21% market share. The deal still needs Chinese and Brazilian regulatory approval. ( SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST )

Taiwan says its ties with Paraguay remain unaffected after the resignation of President Santiago Peña, a close ally, amid a bank collapse. Paraguay is one of 12 countries with formal diplomatic ties to Taipei. Peña visited Taiwan in May, drawing Chinese criticism, and China sanctioned Paraguayan and Belizean ministers last month over Taiwan ties. ( REUTERS )
